title: Repair: an operational timeout becomes a verdict, and Cancel renames a succeeded attempt
description:
Two blockers from the Phase 2 final review (zus). Both are violations of the
epic's OWN x6j guarantee — a substrate failure is never a verdict about the work
— found in the very code that claims it.

Note both are LATENT: usableProfile (internal/reconcile/profiles.go:307) refuses
any profile whose executor is not local-subprocess, so nothing constructs
herdr.Executor outside tests yet. They are what a first real run would hit.

## 1. A slow launch becomes a dead attempt AND a killed live agent

internal/exec/herdr/executor.go:420-425 hands agent.start a startup wait of
DefaultStartupTimeout (60s, executor.go:98) but the call goes through c.call,
bounded by the client's DefaultCallTimeout (30s, client.go:18). A launch that
takes between 30 and 60 seconds aborts CLIENT-side while herdr completes it.

The chain from there: the record is written LaunchConfirmed=false; observe turns
that into terminal `failed`; collect mints missing-result/runner_error, and the
liveness hold is skipped on exactly that record; dispose.go:258 then short-
circuits the liveness question entirely on !LaunchConfirmed and tears the
workspace down WITHOUT asking herdr.

So an operational timeout becomes a verdict about the work, and kills an agent
that is alive and working. Both halves are precisely what x6j forbids.

Fix the timeout relationship first — a call carrying a 60s startup wait cannot
be bounded at 30s — and then the !LaunchConfirmed path: an unconfirmed launch is
the case where liveness is UNKNOWN, which is the one case that must ask herdr
rather than assume.

## 2. Cancel renames a succeeded attempt `cancelled`, forever

internal/exec/herdr/cancel.go:154-189: hasSettled never reads the durable
report. So herdr silence (the default branch) or a still-working agent makes
Cancel write cancel.json over an attempt that has ALREADY REPORTED. `cancelled`
is classify's first case, so a succeeded, mergeable attempt collects as
cancelled from then on.

This is the exact hazard the file's own header says it prevents, and the local
subprocess executor does not have it — tick 0c1 fixed this shape there, and tick
bgr already records that Cancel serves two callers with different needs. Read
both before changing anything.

## Tests

The repair is not done until a test drives each: a launch that takes longer than
the call timeout must not produce a verdict or a teardown, and a cancel arriving
after a report must not rename the verdict.
notes: 2026-09-14 08:56 - runner-state: dispatched on pi/cloudflare GLM-5.3 from base 4a89ebc
acceptance_criteria: A launch slower than the client call timeout does not produce a verdict about the work and does not tear down a live agent: the call's bound accommodates the startup wait, and an unconfirmed launch asks herdr about liveness rather than assuming, proven by a test that drives a launch past the call timeout. Cancel arriving at an attempt that has already reported does not write a cancellation over it, proven by a test that reports first and cancels second and asserts the verdict is unchanged. Neither fix weakens x6j's guarantee or 5hz's reclamation; make test-short green.
